title: Processing of identified data during registration
description: During account registration, the Homeowner provides identified personal data (name, email, contact information) which is processed by the Home Hub. This inherently involves processing of identified information.
assumptions: Standard account registration requires personal identification information

title: Unique identifiers in registration and device enrollment
description: The registration process includes unique identifiers such as email addresses, usernames, and device IDs for cameras/sensors that serve as unique references to the identity of the data subject.
assumptions: Device enrollment requires unique device identifiers

title: Linking through unique identifiers
description: The Home Hub can link all data associated with the homeowner's account and enrolled devices through unique identifiers (account ID, device IDs), enabling comprehensive data linking across the system.
assumptions: System maintains persistent identifiers for accounts and devices

title: Profiling through device enrollment patterns
description: The combination of account data and enrolled camera/sensor devices can be analyzed to profile the homeowner's lifestyle, home layout, security preferences, and daily patterns.
assumptions: Device types and placement patterns can reveal personal information

title: Potentially excessive data type sensitivity
description: Registration and device enrollment may collect more sensitive data types than functionally required, such as detailed device specifications, network topology, or location data beyond what's needed for basic functionality.
assumptions: Device enrollment may collect technical details beyond functional requirements
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific implementation details not provided

title: Data retention beyond functional necessity
description: Registration data and device enrollment information may be retained longer than functionally needed, especially if the homeowner deactivates devices or closes their account.
assumptions: System may retain historical enrollment data
uncertainty_note: Depends on retention policy not specified in flow description

title: Unawareness of full data processing scope
description: The Homeowner may not be fully aware of all personal data being collected, processed, or shared during registration and device enrollment, including metadata and implicit data disclosures.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not comprehensively describe all processing activities

title: Limited control over data processing preferences
description: The Homeowner may lack sufficient control to set preferences or consent regarding how their personal data is processed during and after registration and device enrollment.
assumptions: Registration process may have limited granular consent options

title: Attributable data evidence from registration
description: Registration and device enrollment creates data records that can be attributed to the specific homeowner, preventing them from denying these actions were performed.
assumptions: System maintains audit logs of registration and enrollment activities

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: The registration and device enrollment process may collect more personal data than is actually needed for the stated functionality, potentially violating GDPR data minimization requirements.
assumptions: Data collection scope may exceed functional requirements
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific data fields collected, not fully specified in flow description

title: Processing of identified data in video clips
description: Home Hub processes video clips that contain identifiable information such as faces, license plates, or other personally identifiable visual data before uploading to cloud storage.
assumptions: Video clips contain visual data that can identify individuals

title: Revealing attributes in stored video
description: Cloud video storage contains video clips with revealing attributes (location, time, activities, people present) that support identification of data subjects.
assumptions: Video metadata and content reveal identifying attributes

title: Profiling through video analysis
description: Video clips uploaded from Home Hub can be analyzed to profile individuals based on their activities, movements, and behaviors captured in the recordings.
assumptions: Video content can be analyzed for behavioral patterns

title: Sensitive video data collection
description: Video clips are highly sensitive personal data that may be more sensitive than functionally required, especially if recording areas where people have reasonable expectation of privacy.
assumptions: Video clips may capture sensitive personal data

title: Extended video retention
description: Video clips stored in cloud storage may be retained longer than functionally needed, increasing privacy risks over time.
assumptions: Retention policies may not be clearly defined or limited

title: Cloud provider access to video data
description: Personal video data is made accessible to cloud storage provider and potentially their employees or subcontractors beyond what may be functionally necessary.
assumptions: Cloud storage provider has access to stored video data

title: Unawareness of video recording and storage
description: Individuals captured in video clips may be unaware that their personal data is being collected, processed, and stored in cloud storage.
assumptions: People in video recordings may not know they are being recorded

title: Limited control over video data erasure
description: Data subjects may lack control to request rectification or erasure of their personal data contained in video clips stored in cloud storage.
assumptions: Video data deletion mechanisms may be limited or complex

title: Potential violation of data minimization
description: Storing all recorded video clips in cloud storage may process more personal data than actually needed for the system's functional goals.
assumptions: Not all video clips may be necessary to retain
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific use case and retention policies

title: Potential violation of storage limitation
description: Video clips may be stored in cloud storage longer than needed for the purposes for which they were collected.
assumptions: Retention periods may not be clearly defined or enforced

title: Motion alert contains device/user identifier
description: The motion alert forwarded from the Home Hub likely contains a device identifier or user account ID that uniquely references the data subject, enabling identification of who owns the home hub.
assumptions: Motion alerts typically include device or account identifiers for routing and authentication purposes

title: Motion data reveals revealing attributes
description: Motion alert data reveals when movement occurs in the home, which can indicate occupancy patterns, daily routines, and presence/absence of individuals.
assumptions: Motion sensors detect movement that correlates with human activity in the home

title: Motion patterns enable individual profiling
description: Real-time motion alerts can be analyzed to profile an individual's behavior patterns, daily schedule, and habits based on when and where movement occurs.
assumptions: Motion data over time can reveal behavioral patterns specific to individuals

title: Motion data is sensitive personal data
description: Motion alert data is sensitive as it reveals occupancy and presence information about individuals in their private home environment.
assumptions: Home occupancy data is considered sensitive personal information

title: Real-time alerts process data frequently
description: Real-time motion alerts mean personal data is processed and transmitted more frequently than might be functionally necessary for all use cases.
assumptions: Real-time transmission occurs for every motion event detected

title: Implicit disclosure of occupancy patterns
description: Motion alerts implicitly disclose occupancy patterns and presence/absence information as a side-effect of the explicit motion detection functionality.
assumptions: Motion data inherently reveals when someone is present or absent

title: Data subjects may be unaware of motion tracking
description: Individuals in the home may not be fully aware that their motion is being tracked and transmitted to a mobile app backend in real-time.
assumptions: Home hub users may not fully understand the extent of motion data collection and transmission

title: Limited control over motion data processing
description: Data subjects may lack control over preferences for how motion data is collected, processed, and transmitted to the mobile app backend.
assumptions: Users may have limited granular control over motion alert settings

title: Potential violation of data minimization
description: Real-time transmission of all motion alerts may process more personal data than is functionally necessary, potentially violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Not all motion events may require real-time transmission to the backend
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific system design and whether all motion events are necessary to transmit

title: Profiling through motion detection patterns
description: Motion detection notifications can reveal patterns about when the homeowner is present or absent from their property. Over time, this data can be analyzed to profile the homeowner's daily routines, travel patterns, and occupancy habits.
assumptions: The backend stores or processes motion detection events that can be correlated over time

title: Processing of identified homeowner data
description: The mobile app backend processes identified data to route motion detection notifications to the specific homeowner's device. This requires maintaining a link between the notification and the homeowner's identity.
assumptions: The system uses user accounts or device identifiers to deliver notifications

title: Sensitive occupancy data disclosure
description: Motion detection notifications inherently disclose sensitive information about property occupancy. This reveals when the homeowner is home or away, which could be considered highly sensitive personal data.
assumptions: Motion detection data is treated as personal data under applicable privacy regulations

title: Excessive notification frequency
description: If motion detection triggers notifications frequently (e.g., every motion event), this could constitute excessive processing of personal data beyond what is functionally needed for security awareness.
assumptions: The system may send notifications for every motion event without aggregation or filtering
uncertainty_note: Depends on system configuration - may be configurable

title: Lack of notification preference control
description: The homeowner may lack control over notification preferences such as when to receive alerts, what triggers them, or how frequently they are sent. This limits the data subject's ability to customize their privacy settings.
assumptions: The system may not provide granular notification controls to users
uncertainty_note: Depends on app implementation - many apps do provide controls

title: Potential data minimization violation
description: If the notification includes more information than necessary (e.g., exact timestamps, location details, or motion intensity) beyond what is needed to alert the homeowner, this could violate the data minimization principle.
assumptions: The notification content may include unnecessary details
uncertainty_note: Depends on actual notification content implementation

title: Analytics data shared with predetermined external vendor
description: Device-usage analytics are shared with a cloud analytics vendor (EE3), a predetermined external party. This exposes personal data to more parties than might be functionally necessary, increasing privacy risk through third-party access.
assumptions: The cloud analytics vendor is a known, fixed party in the system architecture

title: Data propagation to external analytics service
description: Personal device-usage data is propagated to an external cloud analytics vendor where it may be processed beyond the original app's functional needs, creating additional privacy exposure.
assumptions: The analytics vendor processes data for purposes beyond what the mobile app backend requires

title: Quasi-identifiers in aggregated analytics
description: Even aggregated device-usage analytics may contain quasi-identifiers (e.g., device type, usage patterns, timestamps) that could be combined with other data to identify individual users.
assumptions: Aggregated analytics retain some granularity that could serve as quasi-identifiers
uncertainty_note: Depends on the actual aggregation level and what attributes are included

title: Individual profiling through usage analytics
description: Device-usage analytics can be analyzed for patterns to profile individual users, linking data to specific individuals based on their usage behavior and patterns.
assumptions: Analytics data contains sufficient detail to enable individual profiling

title: Users unaware of analytics data sharing
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their device-usage analytics are being collected and shared with an external cloud analytics vendor, violating transparency principles.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly disclose third-party analytics sharing

title: Lack of user control over analytics processing
description: Users may lack the ability to set preferences or provide consent regarding how their device-usage analytics are processed and shared with the cloud analytics vendor.
assumptions: The app does not provide granular consent controls for analytics sharing

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Sharing aggregated device-usage analytics with an external vendor may process more personal data than is actually needed for the app's core functionality, potentially violating GDPR data minimization requirements.
assumptions: Analytics sharing is not strictly necessary for core app functionality
uncertainty_note: Depends on whether analytics are functionally required

title: Invalid consent for analytics data processing
description: Personal data collection and processing for analytics sharing may not rely on valid consent if users are not properly informed or if consent is bundled with other terms.
assumptions: Consent mechanisms may not meet GDPR standards for analytics sharing

title: Video content enables individual profiling
description: Stored video clips contain behavioral data that can be analyzed to profile homeowner patterns, habits, and routines through playback history and video content analysis.
assumptions: Video content includes identifiable activities and the system tracks which videos are retrieved and when

title: Video contains identified information
description: Video clips may contain faces, license plates, or other identifying information that directly identifies individuals captured in the footage.
assumptions: Video content includes people or identifiable objects

title: Video metadata contains unique identifiers
description: Video file metadata may contain unique references to the homeowner identity, such as account IDs, device identifiers, or property addresses.
assumptions: Metadata is stored with video files and includes identifying information

title: Video data provides attributable evidence
description: Video clips can be used as evidence to attribute actions or events to specific homeowners, preventing them from denying certain claims about their activities.
assumptions: Video content captures homeowner activities that could be disputed

title: Video is highly sensitive data type
description: Video content is inherently sensitive personal data that reveals intimate details of homeowner life, potentially more than functionally required for playback functionality.
assumptions: Video content includes private home activities

title: Excessive video data volume processed
description: Video files are large in size, and retrieving full video clips may process more data than necessary if only portions are needed for playback.
assumptions: Full video files are retrieved rather than streamed segments

title: Video retention duration may exceed necessity
description: Stored video clips may be retained longer than functionally needed for the homeowner's playback purposes, increasing privacy exposure over time.
assumptions: No clear retention policy limits video storage duration
uncertainty_note: Uncertain about actual retention policies in place

title: Homeowner unaware of video processing details
description: Homeowners may not be fully aware of how their video data is retrieved, processed, and potentially analyzed by the mobile app backend during playback.
assumptions: Privacy notices do not clearly explain backend processing of video data

title: Limited control over video data rectification/erasure
description: Homeowners may lack adequate controls to delete or rectify video data stored in the cloud, especially after retrieval by the backend.
assumptions: Data deletion mechanisms are not user-accessible or comprehensive

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Retrieving and processing full video clips may violate GDPR data minimization if only portions are needed for the playback functionality.
assumptions: Full video retrieval is not strictly necessary for playback
uncertainty_note: Depends on actual technical implementation of video streaming

title: Insufficient data subject controls for video data
description: Homeowners may lack adequate GDPR-compliant controls over their video data, including access, rectification, and erasure rights.
assumptions: User interface does not provide comprehensive data subject rights management
